problem_statement: On an established TCP (stream) socket, recvfrom() and recvmsg() do not fill in the caller's source address. After receiving data, the supplied net_sockaddr structure is left untouched (family 0, zero port) and its length is not set, even though the peer's address is known. recvfrom()/recvmsg() on a stream socket should populate the source address (family, port, and address) from the peer just as accept() does, and for recvmsg() the message's namelen field should reflect the filled-in address length. When userspace is enabled, the updated namelen must also be copied back to the caller after a successful receive.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/net/socket/tcp -s tests/net/socket/tcp/net.socket.tcp -s net.socket.tcp -O twister-out --no-clean -W

verification.reason: The statement fully specifies the required behaviour: recvfrom()/recvmsg() on a stream socket must populate family, port and address from the peer (as accept() does), set addrlen to the address size, set msg_namelen for recvmsg, and copy namelen back in the userspace path. All names used by the tests (NET_AF_INET/INET6, net_sin, net_sin6, net_htons, net_ipv*_is_addr_loopback, struct net_sockaddr_in/in6, msg_namelen, addrlen) are existing APIs or test-local constants, and the exact values (sizeof(net_sockaddr_in)/in6, the peer's bound port) are derivable from accept()'s existing behaviour referenced in the statement. No implementation, flaky, or hardware detail is required by the tests.
